Getting Started with qvdr

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd
library(qvdr)

Introduction

The qvdr package reads QVD (QlikView Data) binary files into R tibbles. QVD is the proprietary high-performance columnar format used by QlikView and Qlik Sense to persist in-memory tables to disk. Each QVD file contains:

  • An XML header with table and field metadata
  • A symbol table — per-field dictionaries of all unique values
  • A bit-packed record matrix — rows encoded as compressed indices into the symbol dictionaries

qvdr parses all three sections, with a C++ backend (via Rcpp) for the bit-extraction inner loop.

Basic usage

Reading a QVD file 

df <- read_qvd("path/to/file.qvd")

This returns a tibble with typed columns:

Qlik type / tag R type
INTEGER integer
REAL, FIX double
$date tag Date
$timestamp tag POSIXct
String / ASCII character

Selecting columns

Load only the columns you need — this skips bit-extraction for unneeded fields:

df <- read_qvd("Sales.qvd", col_select = c("SalesDate", "Amount", "Region"))

Limiting rows

Preview the first N rows without loading the entire file:

df <- read_qvd("Sales.qvd", n_max = 1000)

Suppressing progress output 

df <- read_qvd("Sales.qvd", verbose = FALSE)

Inspecting QVD files without loading data

Three lightweight functions read only the XML header (typically a few KB), making them very fast even for large files:

List field names 

qvd_fields("Sales.qvd")
#> [1] "SalesDate"  "ProductID"  "Region"     "Amount"     "Quantity"

Full metadata 

meta <- qvd_metadata("Sales.qvd")
meta$n_records
#> [1] 4823917
meta$table_name
#> [1] "Sales"
meta$fields
#>       name    type         tags num_symbols bit_width
#> 1 SalesDate    REAL        $date        1096         11
#> 2 ProductID INTEGER             2048         11
#> 3    Region   ASCII              4          3
#> 4    Amount    REAL              -          -
#> 5  Quantity INTEGER             200          8

Schema with R types and distinct counts 

schema <- qvd_schema("Sales.qvd")
print(schema)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   name      r_type  qvd_type tags   n_distinct bit_width
#>   <chr>     <chr>   <chr>    <chr>       <int>     <int>
#> 1 SalesDate Date    REAL     $date        1096        11
#> 2 ProductID integer INTEGER  ""           2048        11
#> 3 Region    character ASCII  ""              4         3
#> 4 Amount    double  REAL     ""           5831        13
#> 5 Quantity  integer INTEGER  ""            200         8

Type coercion options

Keep everything as character

Useful for quick inspection or when you want to handle types yourself:

df <- read_qvd("Sales.qvd", numeric_as_num = FALSE)
# All columns are character

Keep integers as double 

df <- read_qvd("Sales.qvd", int_as_int = FALSE)
# Integer fields returned as double instead

Working with dates

Qlik stores dates as days since 1899-12-30 (Excel-compatible serial numbers). qvdr automatically converts fields tagged $date to R Date objects and $timestamp fields to POSIXct:

df <- read_qvd("Orders.qvd")
class(df$OrderDate)
#> [1] "Date"

class(df$CreatedAt)
#> [1] "POSIXct" "POSIXt"

Performance

qvdr is designed for large files. The bit-extraction loop runs in C++, and the entire data section is read in a single readBin() call to avoid per-record I/O overhead.

Typical throughput on a modern laptop:

File size Records Fields Time
50 MB 1M 10 ~1.5 s
200 MB 1M 40 ~4 s
500 MB 5M 20 ~10 s

Use col_select to read only the columns you need — this proportionally reduces both memory and CPU usage.

Troubleshooting

“Failed to parse QVD XML header” The file may be truncated or created by a very old version of QlikView. Try opening the file in QlikView/Qlik Sense and re-saving it.

Unexpected NA values Qlik uses index 0 (with a bias of −1) as the null sentinel. If you see more NAs than expected, check whether the field has HasUndefined: true in the raw XML header (qvd_metadata(path)$raw_xml).

Wrong date values Dates are stored as days since 1899-12-30. If your date column is tagged $date in Qlik but appears as a numeric in R, it may be missing the tag in the QVD. Cast manually: as.Date(df$MyDate, origin = "1899-12-30").
